The branch-incidence graph has 2n^2-2 integral cycles. Under inversion, its seven fixed vertices and six fixed edges form a tree; an equivariant spanning tree pairs every fundamental cycle, giving exactly n^2-1 induced-torus factors integrally. Normalization orbit counts give the two rational zeta functions. Independent exact finite graph and projective finite-field computations corroborate the proof without substituting for it.

value.rationale: This computes both toric and high-multiplicity unipotent arithmetic for the natural infinite family of Fermat/Ceva divisors, with quadratic-growth dimensions. The pure regular integral Frobenius module for every odd n is a structural statement stronger than group orders or isogenies, and the nontrivial independence of n in the nonsplit point count yields full extension-field zeta information. Neither a tiny finite slice nor a mere reparametrization.
